title: LLM-driven Imitation of Subrational Behavior : Illusion or Reality?

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting the LLM to impersonate children of different ages (2 to 5 years old) in a simulated Stanford Marshmallow Experiment to evaluate how age impacts self-control and delayed gratification.

Simulating a 'double or nothing' gamble based on Prospect Theory to evaluate human-like subrational decision-making under risk, specifically loss aversion, risk aversion over gains, and risk-seeking over losses.
Prompting the LLM to impersonate students with varying GPAs in an academic deadline scenario to measure procrastination, present-bias, and quasi-hyperbolic discounting.
Simulating the Ultimatum Game to evaluate whether an LLM-simulated human responder rejects unfair monetary splits, demonstrating bounded rationality and human social preferences.
